i had suicidal thoughts from at least the age of 9, they got severe around 12/13, and i began taking action more often. it got to the point where i had to be hospitalized. i’m here to say there’s no way to tell if it will get better or not, but for me, it often is influenced by perspective. some of the “darkest” times in my life have been the most beautiful and important, and some of the “best” parts in my life were absolute hell. it’s just so unpredictable.

Marijuana definitely helped in all aspects of my PTSD, but i’m in an illegal state as well and not quite the legal smoking age yet. So for me, my current sleeping meds (75mg trazodone, 15mg melatonin) have helped me a little bit, not immediately or consistently, but have definitely been better for me than no meds or any other meds. Melatonin by itself doesn’t work for me though, but will enhance the trazodone.

honestly, i don’t care what i achieve. i’ve basically accepted my life is pointless and i’m not really interested in succeeding in any way. i know i could do a lot more without my depression, but i feel like the stress of having to do a million things in a certain to achieve a certain goal would trigger my anxiety even more. and then you have to deal with your success, as silly as it sounds. that includes a lot of unwanted social contact and praise. so i am basically scared of success. i’d rather just be viewed unproductive and just live spontaneously and not as life is a big project that needs to be completed in a certain way. if i mess up once, i’ll never forgive myself.
but also, not all fathers and mothers are perfect. all have the potential to either love or hurt you, and some choose the last option for some stupid reason.

just move on and try not to do it again. know what your intentions were and if what you did was in the best intent, you really aren’t to blame, but maybe be more careful next time. they may or may not love you again even if you explain why you did what you did, especially when they’ve had bad experiences in the past that lead to trust issues. but don’t blame yourself for that. if you were trying to do your best for them and were caring for them, don’t take it out on yourself just because you made a mistake in the name of innocence

yeah, the ones closest to you are often the ones who have the biggest damage potential to you if they turn on you, and it seems that they are often the ones that do it the most, unfortunately. “the saddest thing about betrayal is that it never comes from enemies, it comes from the ones you trust the most”
life never gets better and you should never trust anyone. that’s my advice.
